## Selected publications

<div class="pub-card" markdown="0">
  <img src="images/pubs/anokhin2026fastweights.png" alt="Learned refinement of a selected key-value memory slot" class="pub-thumb">
  <div class="pub-body" markdown="0">
  <div class="pub-title">[Fast Weights Recurrent Transformer](https://openreview.net/forum?id=Sl5mOMfm8R)</div>
  <div class="pub-authors">**Ivan Anokhin**, Daria Yasafova, Tianyu Zhao, Irina Rish, Sebastian Risi</div>
  <div class="pub-meta"> NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Long-Context Foundation Models </div>
  <div class="pub-meta">[[PDF](files/fast-weights-recurrent-transformer.pdf)]</div>
  <div class="pub-desc">We introduce a recurrent Transformer with learned, sparse updates to a fixed-size key-value memory. Compared with FIFO-based recurrent Transformers, it improves FineWeb language modeling at small memory sizes, learns associative recall faster, and improves needle-in-a-haystack retrieval.</div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="pub-card" markdown="0">
  <img src="images/pubs/anokhin2026temporal.png" alt="Parallel experts with recurrent state carried between steps" class="pub-thumb">
  <div class="pub-body" markdown="0">
  <div class="pub-title">[Temporal Recurrence Favors Fewer Layers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12531)</div>
  <div class="pub-authors">**Ivan Anokhin**, Johan Obando-Ceron, Irina Rish, Sebastian Risi</div>
  <div class="pub-meta"> Preprint, 2026 </div>
  <div class="pub-meta">[[PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.12531), [Code](https://github.com/avecplezir/fewer-layers-with-rec)]</div>
  <div class="pub-desc">We study how temporal recurrence changes the best allocation of compute along three axes: depth, width, and the number of experts. On Sokoban and FineWeb language modeling, the best observed recurrent models use substantially fewer layers with comparable or better performance under approximately the same per-step compute.</div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="pub-card" markdown="0">
  <img src="images/pubs/ralambomihanta2025learning2.png" alt="Cascading Eligibility Traces thumbnail" class="pub-thumb">
  <div class="pub-body" markdown="0">
  <div class="pub-title">[Learning From the Past with Cascading Eligibility Traces](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.14598)</div>
  <div class="pub-authors">Tokiniaina Raharison Ralambomihanta\*, **Ivan Anokhin**\*, Roman Pogodin\*, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou, Jonathan Cornford, Blake Aaron Richards</div>
  <div class="pub-meta"> ICLR 2026 </div>
  <div class="pub-meta">[[PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.14598), [Code](https://github.com/avecplezir/CET), [Poster](images/pubs/cet_poster.png)]</div>
  <div class="pub-desc">We show how to handle delayed credit assignment in an online, bio-plausible fashion by employing SSMs to retain past activations. We demonstrate the applicability of our method on computer vision and RL tasks. The design is friendly to on-device learning and Streaming RL. </div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="pub-card" markdown="0">
  <img src="images/pubs/anokhin2025handling.png" alt="Handling Delay in Real-Time RL thumbnail" class="pub-thumb">
  <div class="pub-body" markdown="0">
  <div class="pub-title">[Handling Delay in Real-Time Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.23478)</div>
  <div class="pub-authors">**Ivan Anokhin**, Rishav Rishav, Matthew Riemer, Stephen Chung, Irina Rish, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou</div>
  <div class="pub-meta"> ICLR 2025 </div>
  <div class="pub-meta"> [[PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.23478), [Code](https://github.com/avecplezir/realtime-agent), [Blog post](https://mila.quebec/en/article/real-time-reinforcement-learning), [Poster](images/pubs/realtime_poster.png)] </div>
  <div class="pub-desc">We address real-time RL by pipelining layer computations and handling observation delay. We show it leads to faster inference and competitive performance on MuJoCo and MinAtar. The design is also friendly to on-device inference.</div>
  </div>
</div>
